pr_title: admission: incorporate L0 size into overload score
pr_body:
Small ingests happening at a high rate can elevate the sub-level count when small memtables need to be flushed (as observed in a clearrange roachtest). This causes admission control to restrict user-facing traffic, even when the bytes in L0 are modest and can all be compacted away very quickly.

This PR updates the scoring logic to add a max and min sub-level bound. The max is the L0 bytes divided by admission.l0_min_size_per_sub_level, where the latter defaults to 5MB. The min is the sub-level count divided by 3.

Fixes #109207

Epic: none

Release note (ops change): Cluster setting
admission.l0_min_size_per_sub_level is introduced, which reduces the probability of admission control throttling when there is a sequence of small memtable flushes or tiny files ingested into L0.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/109332)

issue_context.title: admission: discount sub-levels when L0 bytes are small
issue_context.body:
We have seen an example (in a clearrange roachtest) where small ingests (likely ranges that have shrunk and being merged) happen at a high rate (since they are small, not many bytes needed to be transferred to the node), resulting in 6+ flushes/s (since these ingests overlap with the memtable). This increases the sub-level count quickly, causing admission control to throttle user-facing work.

The following is an example of a sequence of such ingests, which started with an empty L0, and caused sub-level count to increase to 15+. We do want to use the latest state of L0, since smoothing would delay the reaction to overload, but in this case there isn't a real overload since these bytes can be compacted out of L0 is a few seconds. We should discount the sub-level count based on the bytes in L0 to prevent overreaction in admission control.
